title: Mannens datter og kjerringens datter
world: Present-day rural Norway. At home: a red house on a hillside, with a garden, an old stone well without a lid and an old plank outbuilding that was once a pigsty. The stepmother sells hand-spun yarn online. At the bottom of the well lies another world: an endless summer meadow with no houses or power lines, crossed by an old-fashioned fence of woven brushwood twigs, with an apple tree and a long pole by its trunk. Far across it lies a farm that looks too ordinary. The old woman lives there with her daughter, a younger copy of her with the same hooked nose. The sieve is a round wooden frame with a mesh bottom. The three small chests are gaudy like souvenirs, red, green and blue, with heavy old locks; three tiny crosses are scratched into the lock of the blue one.
palette: Two worlds. At home: a warm June afternoon on a green hillside, with low sun on the old stone well, and later the dusk-lit living room. Below the well: an endless meadow in hazy, timeless summer light, full of flowers and bumblebees; the too-ordinary farm silent under a flat white sky; a dim cowshed. At the end, an old outbuilding glowing gold through every crack. Accents: the Girl's blue bandana and dress, a mustard-yellow hoodie, and the red, green and blue chests.

cast.name: Fars datter
cast.description: Stille og arbeidsom stedatter som møter urett med ro, løser umulige oppgaver med hjelp fra naturen, og velger riktig kiste uten å la seg blende.
cast.look: A slim, kind girl of about sixteen, a little small for her age, with a narrow, gentle face, big grey eyes, a small nose, pink cheeks and a quiet, steady look. Her light-brown wavy hair falls to her shoulders from under a blue cotton bandana knotted at the nape of her neck. She wears a plain blue pinafore dress over a white T-shirt and scuffed green rubber boots.
cast.portrait: Background: the endless summer meadow at the bottom of the well.

cast.name: Mors datter
cast.description: Bortskjemt og aggressiv, tramper over alt som ber om omtanke, avviser hjelpen hun får, og velger den mest glorete kista—med katastrofale følger.
cast.look: A sturdy, broad-shouldered girl of about sixteen with a broad, square face, a heavy jaw, full lips pushed out in a sulk, a wide flat nose, small dark eyes under heavy black eyebrows drawn together in a scowl, and a big, bushy cloud of black frizzy hair tied on top with a red scrunchie. She wears a pink T-shirt, light-wash jeans and chunky white trainers, with a phone in a glittery case sticking out of her back pocket.
cast.portrait: Background: the garden of the red house, with the old stone well.

cast.name: Stemoren
cast.description: Kontrollerende og bitter voksen som favoriserer sin egen datter, skyver stedatteren ut av hjemmet og forsøker å gjøre belønning til noe hun kan stjele.
cast.look: A short, stout, bossy woman of about forty-five with a big, doughy face, heavy cheeks, a small snub nose, small cold black eyes, a sour little mouth and frizzy black hair streaked with grey, bundled into a big messy knot on top of her head. She wears a dark-plum hand-knitted cardigan over a black linen dress, with a large round silver brooch at her collar, and always has her phone in her hand, ready to take pictures.
cast.portrait: Background: skeins of earth-coloured yarn by the old stone well.

cast.name: Den gamle kvinnen på gården
cast.description: En kald, beregnende matmor i en «for vanlig» og altfor stille gård, som setter folk på prøver og tilbyr tre kister som lønn—en test av karakter, ikke arbeid.
cast.look: A big, heavy, barrel-shaped old woman, a head taller than a grown woman and twice as broad, with a wrinkled, sallow face, a very long, knobbly, hooked nose, one thick bushy grey eyebrow straight across her forehead, small squinting black eyes, a sour down-turned mouth and a wart on her chin. Her grey hair is pulled back tight. She wears a dark-red shawl over a charcoal-grey cardigan, a long dark skirt and huge black rubber clogs, and a tufted cow's tail peeks out below the skirt.
cast.portrait: Background: the white farmhouse of the too-ordinary farm.

cast.name: Småfuglene
cast.description: En liten fugleflokk som hvisker konkrete råd ved brønner og fjøs, og fungerer som historiens samvittighet: de hjelper den som lytter og vender seg bort fra den som slår.
cast.look: A small flock of exactly six identical tiny songbirds, blue tits no bigger than a plum: round and fluffy, with a sky-blue cap, wings and tail, a lemon-yellow breast, white cheeks with a thin black stripe through each eye, a short black beak, shiny black bead eyes and thin grey legs. They always stay close together and sing with their beaks wide open.
cast.portrait: Background: the rim of a stone well in hazy summer light.

cast.name: Kua
cast.description: Ei brandet ku på enga med ei trebolle på hornene. Hun vil bli melket, og siden gjemmer hun Fars datter under juret sitt.
cast.look: A big, gentle, plump cow with a brindled coat of dark brown and black streaks over reddish brown, long curved cream-coloured horns, big soft brown eyes with long lashes, a wet pink nose, a calm, friendly face and a swishing tail with a white tuft. Her udder is huge and round, and a wooden bowl hangs by a leather thong from her horns.

cast.name: Væren
cast.description: En vær som er mer ull enn vær. Han vil bli klipt, og siden gjemmer han Fars datter under ullskjerfet hun surret rundt halsen hans.
cast.look: A big, round ram who is more wool than ram: his creamy-white wool is so long and thick that it trails behind him like a bridal veil. He has a black face, black legs, big curly golden-brown horns, sleepy half-closed amber eyes and a soft, silly smile, and a pair of wool shears hangs from one of his horns.

places.name: the Meadow
places.look: An endless summer meadow at the bottom of a well, with no houses, roads or power lines anywhere: tall, soft green grass full of clover, buttercups, harebells and bumblebees under a hazy sky. A faint path runs across it past an old-fashioned fence of woven brushwood twigs, like one in a folk museum, and an old apple tree with a long pole leaning against its trunk.

places.name: the Too-Ordinary Farm
places.look: A farm that looks a little too ordinary, under a flat white sky: a white two-storey farmhouse, a red barn, a bare flagpole with no flag, a gravel yard with an old stone well and a big wooden tub beside it, and no tractor, no dog, no car and nobody about. Everything is neat and silent.

places.name: the Farm Kitchen
places.look: The kitchen of an old farmhouse, plain and spotless: white-painted wooden walls, a scrubbed pine kitchen table with four chairs, an old enamel wood stove, a deep windowsill under a small window looking out on the yard, a rag rug and a door to a dim hallway with coat pegs.

cover.prompt: In the endless summer Meadow, the Girl walks along a faint path carrying the small blue chest under her arm and smiles up at the Little Birds fluttering round her head. Beside the path stand the brindled Cow with the wooden bowl on her horns and the Ram, freshly sheared, with a thick scarf of wool wound round his neck, both watching her kindly. Behind them stands an apple tree with straight, light branches.
cover.caption: Fars datter var snill mot alle hun møtte på enga.
cover.alt: Fars datter går over ei endeløs eng med en blå kiste under armen, og småfuglene flyr rundt hodet hennes. Ved stien står ei brandet ku og en nyklipt vær med ull rundt halsen, og bak dem står et epletre.

illustrations.prompt: A warm June afternoon in the garden of a red house on a hillside, by an old stone well without a lid. The Stepsister spins shiny, pale flax fast on a drop spindle with a smug look, while the Girl holds a paper bag of stiff black pig bristles and just looks at them. The Stepmother stands in front of them with her phone held up, looking for the right angle for her pictures. Low sun on the grass.
illustrations.caption: Stemoren sto med mobilen oppe og lette etter vinkelen.
illustrations.alt: Ved en gammel steinbrønn i hagen spinner Mors datter blankt lin, mens Fars datter ser ned i en pose med stiv bust. Stemoren står foran dem med mobilen oppe og tar bilder.

illustrations.anchor: Hun lå på ryggen i gresset
illustrations.prompt: Low view across the Meadow: the Girl lies on her back in tall, soft grass full of flowers and bumblebees, propped up on her elbows, staring up in astonishment at a clear blue sky with no well-hole in it anywhere. The Meadow stretches away forever in every direction, with no houses and no power lines.
illustrations.caption: Så langt hun kunne se, var det bare eng: gress, blomster, humler.
illustrations.alt: Fars datter ligger på ryggen i høyt gress fullt av blomster og humler og ser forundret opp på en blå himmel der brønnhullet skulle vært. Enga strekker seg så langt øyet rekker.

illustrations.anchor: Fars datter hadde aldri melket en ku.
illustrations.prompt: In the Meadow, the Girl crouches beside the big brindled Cow with her hands on the teats, and the milk squirts into the wooden bowl almost by itself; she looks surprised at how easy it is. The Cow's udder is huge and round, and the Cow chews calmly and looks back at her. Bumblebees in the clover, hazy summer light.
illustrations.caption: Bare hun tok i spenene, sprutet melka ned i bollen. Kua gjorde visst det meste selv.
illustrations.alt: Fars datter sitter på huk ved den store, brandete kua og melker. Melka spruter ned i en trebolle nesten av seg selv, og kua tygger rolig og ser på henne.

illustrations.prompt: In the Meadow, the Girl sits in the grass with the big Ram lying still across her lap and shears him with practised, careful hands, like someone who has done it every spring for years. Half of him is already neatly clipped, and the rest of his long wool trails out behind him across the grass like a bridal veil. A bundle of the finest wool lies beside her.
illustrations.caption: Sauer kunne hun. Hun hadde klippet stemorens sju hver vår i tre år.
illustrations.alt: Den store væren ligger musestille i fanget til Fars datter, og hun klipper ham med stødige hender. Ulla hans ligger utover gresset som et brudeslør.

illustrations.anchor: En gammel kvinne åpnet døra før Fars datter rakk å banke.
illustrations.prompt: The Too-Ordinary Farm under a flat white sky, silent, with nobody about and only small birds on the barn roof. The Girl has just stepped up to the front door of the white farmhouse with her hand raised to knock, but the door is already open: the Old Woman stands in it, huge, looking down at her. Behind her in the dim hallway, her daughter stares without blinking.
illustrations.caption: En gammel kvinne åpnet døra før Fars datter rakk å banke.
illustrations.alt: Fars datter står foran et helt vanlig hvitt våningshus med hånden løftet for å banke, men døra er allerede åpen. Der står en stor, gammel kvinne med mørkerødt sjal, og bak henne stirrer dattera hennes.

illustrations.anchor: Den gamle kvinnen så lenge på soldet.
illustrations.prompt: In the Farm Kitchen, the Old Woman holds up the round wooden sieve, its mesh smeared with grey clay and stuck with straws, brimming with water that does not leak, and stares at it for a long time with narrowed eyes. The Girl, now wearing a mustard-yellow hoodie over her blue dress, stands by the door with her hands behind her back, saying nothing.
illustrations.caption: «Det der har du ikke funnet på selv», sa hun.
illustrations.alt: Den gamle kvinnen holder opp soldet, som er tettet med leire og strå og fullt av vann, og ser lenge på det. Fars datter står ved døra i en sennepsgul hettegenser og sier ingenting.

illustrations.anchor: Fars datter visste mye om ull.
illustrations.prompt: By the stone well in the yard of the Too-Ordinary Farm, the Girl, in the mustard-yellow hoodie, lifts a heavy, dripping armful of wool out of the big wooden tub, and it has come out white as new snow, while the water left in the tub is inky black. On the rim of the tub, the Little Birds sing. Flat white sky, the silent farmhouse behind.
illustrations.caption: Da hun løftet den opp igjen, var den hvit som nysnø.
illustrations.alt: Ved brønnen på gården løfter Fars datter ulla opp av en stor stamp. Vannet er svart, men ulla er blitt hvit som nysnø. På kanten av stampen sitter småfuglene og synger.

illustrations.prompt: In the Farm Kitchen, three small chests, gaudy as souvenirs, stand on the kitchen table: a red one, a green one and a blue one, each with a heavy old lock. The Girl, in the mustard-yellow hoodie, bends close over the blue one, where three tiny crosses are scratched into the lock, and picks it up. The Little Birds sit packed together on the windowsill, singing softly. The Old Woman watches from across the table with her arms folded.
illustrations.caption: I låsen på den blå var det risset tre små kors. Hun tok den blå.
illustrations.alt: Tre glorete kister står på kjøkkenbordet: en rød, en grønn og en blå. Fars datter løfter den blå, som har tre små kors risset i låsen. I vinduskarmen synger småfuglene, og den gamle kvinnen ser på med armene i kors.

illustrations.anchor: Greinene senket seg rundt henne som et forheng.
illustrations.prompt: Under the old apple tree in the Meadow, the Girl crouches in green shade with the blue chest in her arms, holding her breath, while the leafy branches hang down all round her like a curtain. Through a gap in the leaves, just outside, two pairs of big, heavy, clumpy shoes and the hems of two long dark skirts have stopped on the path. Sunlight flickers through the leaves.
illustrations.caption: Gjennom bladene så hun to par tunge sko stanse.
illustrations.alt: Fars datter sitter gjemt under de hengende greinene på epletreet med den blå kista i armene. Gjennom en glipe i bladene ser hun to par tunge sko som har stanset på stien.

illustrations.anchor: Hun lå i det varme gresset under kua
illustrations.prompt: In the Meadow, the Girl lies flat in the warm grass under the belly of the big brindled Cow, hugging the blue chest, her cheek pressed to the ground and her eyes wide. The Cow stands squarely over her, chewing, and gazes innocently down the path, where the Old Woman comes stomping towards them in the distance, her dark-red shawl flapping.
illustrations.caption: Hun lå i det varme gresset under kua og kjente hjertet dunke mot bakken.
illustrations.alt: Fars datter ligger i gresset under magen til kua og holder den blå kista tett inntil seg. Kua står rolig og tygger, og langt borte på stien kommer den gamle kvinnen.

illustrations.prompt: In the Meadow, the old brushwood fence has turned furious: it spits and crackles like juniper on a bonfire and rears up, twig by twig, higher than the Old Woman and denser than a wall. She stands on the near side, looking up at it for a long time with her hands hanging at her sides. Deep among the twigs at the bottom, a scrap of blue bandana shows where the Girl lies hidden.
illustrations.caption: Gjerdet reiste seg, kvist for kvist, høyere enn den gamle kvinnen og tettere enn en mur.
illustrations.alt: Risgjerdet har reist seg høyere enn den gamle kvinnen og tettere enn en mur, og det freser og knitrer. Hun står foran det og ser opp. Dypt inne mellom kvistene skimtes en blå bandana.

illustrations.anchor: Lyset sivet ut gjennom sprekkene i veggene
illustrations.prompt: Late evening in the garden of the red house. The old plank outbuilding glows, golden light seeping out through every crack in its walls. Through the open door, gold, silver, jewellery and shining fabrics hang from the walls and beams, spilling out of the open blue chest on a stool, and the Girl stands in the middle of it all. In the doorway, the Stepmother and the Stepsister have stopped dead, their faces lit gold, mouths open.
illustrations.caption: Hvor hadde hun vært? Hva slags jobb var det? Hvem betalte sånn?
illustrations.alt: Det gamle uthuset lyser av gull. Inne henger gull, sølv og smykker på vegger og bjelker rundt den åpne blå kista, og Fars datter står midt i det. I døra står stemoren og Mors datter og gaper.

illustrations.anchor: «Hva bryr jeg meg om en kvisthaug», sa Mors datter
illustrations.prompt: In the Meadow, the Stepsister stamps across the old brushwood fence so that it creaks and snaps under her chunky trainers, twigs flying, while she holds her phone high above her head in one hand, looking for coverage, with a scowl. Further along the path, the brindled Cow waits in the grass with her heavy udder and the wooden bowl on her horns.
illustrations.caption: «Hva bryr jeg meg om en kvisthaug», sa Mors datter.
illustrations.alt: Mors datter tramper over risgjerdet så det knaker og brekker, og holder mobilen høyt over hodet for å få dekning. Lenger borte venter kua.

illustrations.prompt: By the stone well in the yard of the Too-Ordinary Farm, the Stepsister stands holding the empty wooden sieve, the water pouring straight through its mesh, her other hand muddy with grey clay and a furious scowl on her face. The Little Birds scatter up into the flat white sky, unhurt, and a splat of clay has hit the rim of the well where they sat.
illustrations.caption: Hun kastet en neve leire etter fuglene så de fløy.
illustrations.alt: Mors datter står ved brønnen med et tomt sold som vannet renner rett gjennom. Hånda er full av leire, og småfuglene flyr sin vei. På brønnkanten er det en leireklatt der de satt.

illustrations.prompt: In the Farm Kitchen, the three gaudy chests stand on the kitchen table. The Stepsister snatches up the red one, which glints the most, with a greedy grin. On the windowsill, the Little Birds, only three of them now, sing their warning, but she does not listen. The Old Woman watches her with a thin, sour smile.
illustrations.caption: Mors datter tok den røde. Den glinset mest.
illustrations.alt: Mors datter griper den røde kista på kjøkkenbordet, for den glinser mest. I vinduskarmen synger småfuglene, færre nå, og den gamle kvinnen smiler surt.

illustrations.anchor: Ut veltet mark og padder og slim og kryp
illustrations.prompt: The living room of the red house at dusk. The red chest stands open on the floor between two armchairs, and out of it pours a long, glistening stream of worms, toads, snails and creepy-crawlies, spreading across the floor, up the armchairs and behind the pictures on the wall. The Stepsister claps both hands over her mouth, eyes bulging, and the Stepmother stands as stiff as a post.
illustrations.caption: Ut veltet mark og padder og slim og kryp.
illustrations.alt: Den røde kista står åpen på stuegulvet, og ut velter mark, padder og kryp som sprer seg over gulvet og opp i lenestolene. Mors datter holder seg for munnen, og stemoren står stiv som en stokk.
